meaning: Phone settings that let apps use your location, camera, mic, or contacts.
clues: They are phone settings that control what an app may use.
They can let an app use, or block, your camera, microphone, or contacts.
You can review them for each app in your phone settings.
Giving less access can limit what an app can do.
The name has two words, and the second means approvals.
assumes: Location services let a phone or app use location information
Screen time limits when or how long apps can be used
Do Not Disturb silences calls and alerts for a while

decoys.meaning: A phone feature that uses signals to figure out where the phone is.
A phone feature that shows or limits how long you use apps.
A phone setting that turns off calls and alerts for a while.

exchange.speaker: bud
exchange.text: Try opening one app in your phone settings and look at what it can access. Turn off access it does not need.

exchange.speaker: floyd
exchange.text: You should know what you hand over. We read the label before giving a shop our home address.

exchange.speaker: bud
exchange.text: You can change a choice later if you decide the app needs that access.

sources.name: FTC, How Websites and Apps Collect and Use Your Information

blank.sentence: I opened my phone settings and turned off the camera access an app did not need. Those settings are called ___.

why: Apps do not need to reach everything, so give them only what they need.
short: Settings for what apps can use

situations.text: An app has asked to use your contacts, and it does not need them. You turn that access off.
situations.why: Turn off access an app does not need. You can change it later.
